figure2_ffn_selection.why: magnitude is the recommended FFN recipe (ROADMAP, v0.7.0 selection defaults) and is the selection the exp39/exp46 latency grid timed. Figure 1's ViT panel plots the random arm for a different reason: its three panels are read for ordering and must vary only the structure. The two arms differ by 0.43pp at 25%, which is larger than either one's seed range, so this is a stated difference and not an inconsistency to be reconciled.

captions_for_latex.fig_cost_by_structure: Cost of removing about the same parameter budget, by the structure removed. Bars are the mean over seeds and whiskers the range over seeds, not an interval: below ten draws the campaign reports a range. Every cost is the arm minus the dense control trained for the same budget on the same seed. A ViT cost is points of top-1 lost and is negative; an OPT cost is perplexity gained and is positive. The ViT axis is inverted so that a longer bar is a worse arm in every panel. The units differ, so the panels are read for ordering and never for magnitude. The FFN arm is randomly selected in all three panels.
captions_for_latex.fig_quality_vs_latency: Quality against measured latency for the physically sliced ViT arms. Marker area is the parameter count; whiskers are the range over seeds. CPU speedups are the three-pass re-measurement: two cells of the single-pass grid did not survive being measured again, and a cell whose three passes disagree by more than 5 percent is marked unstable. The dense reference is 1.0 by construction and is not marked, although its own three passes span 8.3 percent. Unstructured and 2:4 arms are absent because they are masked, not sliced, and give no speedup without a sparse kernel. The FFN arms here (mlp25, mlp50, head50_mlp50) are MAGNITUDE-selected, which is the recommended FFN recipe and the selection the latency grid timed; figure 1's ViT panel plots the randomly selected FFN arm instead, so that its three panels vary the structure and not the selection. Magnitude costs -0.82pp at 25% and random -1.25pp, both against the same matched 2-epoch control, so the two figures differ by 0.43pp on this arm by design and not by accident.
